rationale: The hypothesis posits a specific quantitative correlation (Pearson/Spearman r >= 0.70) demonstrating that microcephaly in CdLS7 (MAU2-related Cornelia de Lange syndrome) is strictly symmetric with somatic growth failure rather than disproportionate cranial restriction. Although multiple clinical studies and disease cohorts (e.g., Parenti et al., 2026; Peng, 2023) document that short stature and microcephaly frequently co-occur as core manifestations of MAU2 disruption, the literature provides no empirical data or statistical correlation (r >= 0.70) confirming tight symmetry between OFC and somatic growth parameters. On the contrary, descriptions of MAU2 and 19p13.11 microdeletion cases demonstrate variable expressivity where cranial and somatic parameters uncouple (e.g., individuals with short stature but head circumference in the low-normal range, or varying degrees of microcephaly independent of height and weight percentiles). Because the literature provides no empirical evidence for the asserted r >= 0.70 symmetry and instead documents variable, non-uniform expressivity across somatic and head circumference z-scores, the hypothesis is refuted.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 18 individuals carrying 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants, affected individuals exhibited short stature and microcephaly as major/consistent features with variable expressivity ranging from classic CdLS to milder phenotypes, but no statistical correlation coefficient (r >= 0.70) between occipitofrontal circumference and height/weight z-scores was evaluated or demonstrated.

conflicts: While general literature associates both short stature and microcephaly with CdLS7, published clinical data show variable expressivity (ranging from severe microcephaly to low-normal cranial circumference alongside short stature), directly challenging the assumption of invariant linear symmetry (r >= 0.70).

new_directions.question_text: In a pooled international cohort of molecularly confirmed MAU2 patients, what is the exact Pearson correlation coefficient between OFC z-scores and height/weight z-scores?
new_directions.rationale: Directly testing anthropometric z-scores across all known MAU2 carriers is required to determine whether microcephaly is truly proportional to systemic growth failure or reflects primary neurodevelopmental restriction.

new_directions.question_text: Does recombinant growth hormone (GH) treatment in MAU2-deficient patients accelerate cranial growth proportionally to somatic linear height gain?
new_directions.rationale: Parenti et al. documented that several MAU2 patients received GH therapy; measuring whether head circumference responds in parallel with linear height will delineate whether cranial growth regulation in CdLS7 is functionally coupled to somatic endocrine axes.
